items.h1: Windrose Beginner Guide: Day 1-10 Walkthrough & Tips (2026)

faq.question: What's the best difficulty for a complete beginner?
faq.answer: Calm Waters is the recommended difficulty for players new to survival games. It reduces enemy damage and stress levels, giving you room to learn the mechanics without constant punishment. If you have experience with games like Valheim or Enshrouded, High Seas (the standard experience) is a good starting point.

faq.question: Can I change the difficulty after starting?
faq.answer: No. Difficulty is locked once you create your world. You cannot change it mid-game. If you want to switch difficulties, you must start a new world. Choose carefully during world creation.

faq.question: How do I get my first ship?
faq.answer: Follow the Island quest progression chain : craft a Stone Pickaxe → mine Poor Copper Ore → build a Charcoal Kiln and Smelting Furnace → produce Copper Ingots → build the Weaponsmith Workshop and craft a melee weapon. Upon completing this chain, you receive your first ship for free and unlock the "Rescuing the Crew" and "I Need a Bigger Boat" quests.

faq.question: What happens when I die?
faq.answer: When you die, you drop your items at the location of your death. You can return to that spot to recover them. Be careful — if you die again before recovering your items, the original dropped items may be lost. Fortunately, enemies do not regenerate health when you disengage, so you can retreat and approach fights cautiously.

faq.question: How do I get more inventory space early on?
faq.answer: Craft the Torn Sailcloth Bag at the Workbench. It requires 2 Coarse Fabric + 1 Rope . Both Coarse Fabric and Rope are made from Plant Fiber (3 Plant Fiber each) at the Workbench. Later, you can upgrade to the Sailor Backpack (Lv2 Workbench) and eventually the Bosun Backpack (Lv3 Workbench).

items.description: Windrose first boss guide covering battle strategy, recommended gear, phase tactics, and drops. Complete preparation checklist for the starter-area boss. Updated 2026.
items.h1: Windrose First Boss Guide: Strategy, Tips & Drops (2026)

faq.question: When is the first boss fight?
faq.answer: The first boss is encountered in the starter area after completing initial island quests and crafting Copper-tier equipment.

faq.question: What gear level is recommended?
faq.answer: Minimum: full Copper tools and weapons. At least one melee weapon (Saber recommended) and 10-15 Bandages.

faq.question: Can I fight bosses in co-op?
faq.answer: Yes! Windrose supports 1-8 player co-op. Bosses scale with player count, but having teammates to split aggro makes fights significantly easier.

items.title: Windrose Second Boss Guide: Strategy & Drops (2026) | Windrose Guides
items.description: Windrose second boss guide with strategy tips, recommended gear, phase breakdown, drops, and post-boss progression. Updated 2026.

faq.question: How does the second boss differ from the first?
faq.answer: The second boss introduces multi-phase mechanics, environmental hazards, and requires better stamina management. Expect more complex attack patterns compared to the starter boss.

faq.question: Do I need Iron gear for the second boss?
faq.answer: While Copper gear is viable with skill, Iron weapons significantly reduce the fight duration. At minimum, bring Copper-tier weapons and plenty of healing.

items.title: Windrose Charon's Obols Boss Guide: Strategy, Phases & Drops (2026)
items.description: Complete guide to the Charon's Obols boss fight in Windrose. Learn all three phases, best strategies, ship recommendations, drop tables, and post-battle unlocks. Updated for 2026.
items.h1: Windrose Charon's Obols Boss Guide: Strategy, Phases & Drops (2026)

faq.question: What level should I be for Charon's Obols?
faq.answer: The recommended level is to be confirmed once the game launches. Based on similar boss encounters, you should expect to be at least mid-game with a fully upgraded Brigantine-class ship. Crew should be well-leveled with decent gear.

faq.question: What ship is best for fighting Charon's Obols?
faq.answer: The Brigantine is the recommended ship. It offers the best balance of speed to dodge spectral attacks and firepower to break the ghost ship's armor. The Frigate is too slow for Phase 2 projectiles, while the Sloop lacks the durability and cannon power needed for Phase 3.

faq.question: Can I fight Charon's Obols solo?
faq.answer: Yes, the encounter scales based on crew size. Solo players will face fewer phantom escorts in Phase 1 and Charon's health pool will be reduced. However, solo play makes Phase 3 significantly harder as you will need to manage adds while damaging the boss alone.

faq.question: What happens if I die during the fight?
faq.answer: If you are defeated, you will respawn at the nearest port. Your ship will need repairs and you will lose any consumables used during the attempt. The boss's health resets fully. There is no penalty to retrying beyond the supply cost.

faq.question: Are the drops guaranteed on every clear?
faq.answer: First clear drops are guaranteed as listed. Repeat clears have reduced drop rates, with the legendary Charon's Figurehead having a low chance (estimated 5-10%) on subsequent kills. Obol currency is always awarded.

faq.question: Can I skip Charon's Obols and come back later?
faq.answer: Charon's Obols guards the passage to the Underworld Sea region. You must defeat this boss to progress the main story and access later areas. It cannot be skipped, but you can over-level and return with better gear.

faq.question: Do enemies raid my base?
faq.answer: Yes, enemy factions can raid your base. The frequency and difficulty depend on your faction reputation and base location. Building proper defenses is essential for mid-game survival.

faq.question: What's the best early-game defense?
faq.answer: Start with a simple wood palisade wall and spike traps at your camp entrance. Upgrade to stone walls once you have a reliable Iron supply. The best early defense is a good weapon — enemies can't raid if they're dead.

faq.question: Should I build one big base or multiple small ones?
faq.answer: Early game: multiple small outposts near resources. Mid-game: one permanent centralized base with docks and defenses. Keep a small forward camp when exploring new biomes.

faq.question: Can I move my buildings after placing them?

items.h1: Windrose Beginner Builds: Easy Survivability Setups (2026)

faq.question: What stats should a beginner prioritize in Windrose?
faq.answer: Beginners should prioritize Stamina (for more dodges and attacks) and Health (for survivability). Avoid investing heavily in damage stats early; you gain more from learning enemy patterns and staying alive than from a 5% damage increase.

faq.question: Is the Saber really the best beginner weapon?
faq.answer: Yes. The Saber's balanced stats make it the most forgiving weapon for new players. It works against every enemy type and doesn't require specialized playstyle knowledge like the Rapier or Club.

faq.question: When should I switch to a DPS or tank build?
faq.answer: Switch when you can consistently clear areas without dying and you understand enemy attack patterns. This usually happens around the time you unlock the Smelting Furnace and craft your first Copper Armor set (roughly 5-10 hours into the game).

items.h1: Windrose DPS Builds: Max Damage Rapier & Musket Setups (2026)

faq.question: Which weapon has the highest DPS in Windrose?
faq.answer: The Rapier has the highest sustained DPS due to its very fast attack speed, low stamina cost, and high crit chance. When paired with agility-focused stats and the Musket for opening shots, the Rapier build can melt bosses faster than any other setup.

faq.question: Is DPS build viable for solo play?
faq.answer: Yes, but it's higher risk. DPS builds sacrifice defense for damage, meaning you'll die in fewer hits. This build is recommended for players who have already learned enemy attack patterns and dodge timing. Beginners should start with the Beginner Build first.

faq.question: Rapier or Halberd for DPS?
faq.answer: Rapier wins for sustained single-target DPS. Halberd has higher burst damage per swing but is much slower and stamina-hungry. Against bosses with small punish windows, the Rapier consistently outperforms. Against groups, the Halberd's sweeping attacks may be better.

items.title: Windrose Builds Guide: DPS, Tank & Beginner Setups (2026) | Windrose Guides
items.description: Complete Windrose build guide with community-theorycrafted DPS, tank, and beginner setups. Recommended weapons, armor, stat allocation, and playstyle advice for every build archetype.
items.h1: Windrose Builds Guide: DPS, Tank & Beginner Setups (2026)

headings.text: Build 1: Beginner Bruiser (Recommended for New Players)

faq.question: What is the best build in Windrose?
faq.answer: There is no single "best" build. The Bleed DPS build (Rapier of 1000 Cuts + Reliable Musket) offers the highest damage ceiling but requires skilled dodge timing. The Beginner Bruiser (Cutlass + Pikeman/Conquistador armor) is the safest for new players. Choose based on your comfort with the combat system.

faq.question: Can I switch builds mid-game?
faq.answer: Yes. Respecs are completely free in Windrose. You can reallocate stats and talents at any time with no cost. Craft different weapons and armor sets and swap between builds as needed.

faq.question: Which build is best for co-op?
faq.answer: In co-op, the ideal duo is one Tank (Halberd + Pikeman/Conquistador) to draw aggro and one Bleed DPS (Rapier + Musket) to deal sustained damage. The Beginner build works as a flexible middle-ground in any party.

faq.question: Are these builds final?
faq.answer: No. All builds are based on community theorycrafting during Early Access. Balance patches may shift the meta. Check back after major updates for revised recommendations.

items.title: Windrose Tank Builds: Max Survivability Club & Iron Armor Setups (2026) | Windrose Guides
items.description: Best Windrose tank builds for maximum survivability. Club + Blunderbuss combo, full Iron Armor, health and stamina stat priority. Stagger-lock enemies and survive boss fights.
items.h1: Windrose Tank Builds: Max Survivability Club & Iron Armor Setups (2026)

tables.caption: Tank Build Pros & Cons
rows: Extremely forgiving — survive mistakes that kill DPS builds
Slow kill times — fights take longer
Low mobility — can't chase fast enemies easily
High resource cost for Iron Armor
Great for exploring unknown areas safely
Less satisfying for players who prefer fast-paced combat
Musket is generally better for single-target ranged damage

faq.question: Is tank build viable in Windrose?
faq.answer: Yes. Tank builds are extremely viable, especially for co-op play and exploring new areas. The Club's high stagger damage combined with Iron Armor's defense lets you absorb hits that would kill a DPS build while locking down dangerous enemies.

faq.question: Should I use the Club or Halberd for tanking?
faq.answer: The Club is better for pure tanking due to its blunt damage type that builds stagger faster and its lower stamina cost compared to the Halberd. The Halberd deals more damage and can hit groups, but its very high stamina cost leaves you vulnerable. Club is the safer, more consistent tank weapon.

faq.question: Can tank builds solo bosses?
faq.answer: Yes, but boss fights will take longer. The tank's advantage is that you can survive boss attack patterns that would one-shot lighter builds, giving you more time to learn and react. It's a slow-but-steady approach — ideal for first-time boss attempts.

faq.question: Does the tank build work with the Saber?
faq.answer: Yes, but you lose the Club's stagger advantage. A Saber + Iron Armor setup is essentially the "safe beginner" build upgraded to endgame. It works, but a true tank build leverages the Club's blunt stagger mechanics for maximum control.

items.title: Windrose FAQ: Top 20 Frequently Asked Questions (2026) | Windrose Guides
items.description: Windrose FAQ: answers to the top 20 most-asked questions about copper, gunpowder, workbench upgrades, ships, fast travel, backpacks, difficulty settings, and more. Updated 2026.
items.h1: Windrose FAQ — Top 20 Frequently Asked Questions (2026)

faq.question: 1. How do I get copper in Windrose?
faq.answer: Find the small pickaxe icon on your map to locate Copper Deposit Mines (caves). Enter the cave, use a Stone Pickaxe to mine Poor Copper Ore , then bring it back to your Smelting Furnace. Recipe: 6 Copper Ore + 1 Charcoal = 1 Copper Ingot . Caves often contain Drowned enemies — bring weapons and bandages. Related: Copper Ore Guide — Locations, Uses & Tips

faq.question: 2. How do I upgrade the Workbench to Level 2?
faq.answer: Build a Sawhorse (20 Wood + 10 Copper Ingot) near your Workbench within the same Bonfire radius . The Sawhorse add-on triggers the Lv2 upgrade automatically. For Lv3 , build a Toolbox (10 Wood + 20 Nails + 5 Foothills Iron Ingot) near the Workbench. Some recipes also require you to pick up new materials before they appear in the crafting menu. Related: Workbench Crafting Recipes — All Lv1/Lv2/Lv3

faq.question: 3. How do I get my first ship?
faq.answer: Complete the starting island quests. After you build the Weaponsmith Workshop and craft your first melee weapon (Saber, Rapier, or Club), you'll receive your first ship for free and unlock the "Rescuing the Crew" and "I Need a Bigger Boat" quest chains. Related: Ship Building Guide — Sloop, Brigantine & Frigate

faq.question: 4. How do I fast travel?
faq.answer: Craft a Fast Travel Bell at the Workbench: 10 Copper Ingot + 3 Rope . Place it at your base or any location you want to return to. You can teleport between any placed bells. Rope is crafted from 3 Plant Fiber at the Workbench.

faq.question: 5. How do I get gunpowder early?
faq.answer: The fastest early-game method: on the first Coastal Jungle island, find the Smuggler's Treasure point. Break the wood pile, go downstairs, defeat the Drowned enemy, and open the chest on the right — it contains 10 Gunpowder + 4 Rum Bottles . Also clear Blackbeard Pirate Camps for gunpowder drops. Later, craft it: 10 Sulfur + 20 Ash = 10 Gunpowder at a Millstone (requires reaching Foothills and an Iron Pickaxe for Sulfur). Related: Gunpowder Guide — Early & Late-Game Sources

faq.question: 6. Where do I find clay?
faq.answer: Clay spawns randomly on the map, common on the starting island . Look for large dark soil patches near water or riverbanks. Mine it with a Stone Pickaxe. Used for Clay Pots, Clay Bottles, Charcoal Kiln (25 Wood + 20 Clay), and Smelting Furnace (15 Clay + 30 Stone). Related: Clay Locations & Uses Guide

faq.question: 7. How do I craft a bigger backpack?
faq.answer: Three backpack tiers, crafted at the Workbench: Torn Sailcloth Bag (Lv1): 2 Coarse Fabric + 1 Rope Sailor Backpack (Lv2): 1 Torn Sailcloth Bag + 5 Rough Hide + 2 Copper Ingot Bosun Backpack (Lv3): 1 Sailor Backpack + 5 Tanned Leather + 2 Foothills Iron Ingot Coarse Fabric = 3 Plant Fiber. Rope = 3 Plant Fiber. Both at the Workbench.

faq.question: 8. What's the best difficulty for beginners?
faq.answer: Calm Waters — reduces enemy damage and stress, perfect for first-time players. If you have survival game experience (Rust, Valheim, etc.), choose High Seas for the standard 100% experience. Storm's Edge increases enemy health/damage for challenge seekers. Captain's Choice offers custom sliders up to 500%. Difficulty is locked at world creation.

faq.question: 9. Can I pause the game?
faq.answer: No! Windrose has no pause function at all. Always ensure your surroundings are completely safe before opening menus or inventory. If you need to step away, return to your base or a cleared area first.

faq.question: 10. How do I heal?
faq.answer: Craft Bandages at the Workbench: 1 Coarse Fabric each . Always carry 5-10 bandages and use them before health gets critical. Coarse Fabric = 3 Plant Fiber. For passive healing, eat coconuts (from palm trees) — they restore both hunger and thirst.

faq.question: 11. How many players can play co-op?
faq.answer: The game supports up to 10 players , but the developers recommend 2–4 players for the best experience. Groups of 5–8 may experience performance dips, and 10-player mode is considered experimental. Crew members can operate different ship weapons during naval combat, or split up to explore islands and dungeons together.

faq.question: 12. What are pearls used for?
faq.answer: Right-click on scallop shells dropped by beach enemies — pearls work as emergency ammunition when you run out of gunpowder. They're a useful backup in the early game before you have a steady ammo supply.

faq.question: 13. How do I get more inventory space?
faq.answer: Craft backpack upgrades: Torn Sailcloth Bag → Sailor Backpack (Lv2 Workbench) → Bosun Backpack (Lv3 Workbench). Each tier gives significantly more carrying capacity. See FAQ #7 for full crafting recipes.

faq.question: 14. Can I change difficulty mid-game?
faq.answer: No. Difficulty is locked permanently when you create your world. Choose carefully. To change difficulty, you must create a new world.

faq.question: 15. What happens when I die?
faq.answer: You drop your items at your death location. You can return to recover them. A key advantage: enemies do not regenerate health when they lose aggro, so you can use hit-and-run tactics against tough opponents.

faq.question: 16. How do I build a base?
faq.answer: Press B to enter build mode, Q for fine-tune placement, V for overhead view. You can build almost anywhere. Tip: don't build a giant permanent base early — set up temporary outposts near resource-rich areas. Upgrade your camp via Decoration items to extend the Rested buff duration.

faq.question: 17. How does combat work in Windrose?
faq.answer: Windrose uses Soulslite combat — you must manage Stamina for attacks, blocks, and dodges. Press Ctrl to dodge (has i-frames). Tap block at the precise moment of an enemy strike for a Perfect Block that negates all damage and staggers the enemy. Effective loop: attack 1–2 times → dodge back → wait for enemy approach → heavy/sprint attack. Press T to lock on. You can stack two food buffs simultaneously and respec stats for free at any time.

faq.question: 18. Where do I find iron ore?
faq.answer: Iron ore is found in the Foothills region, reached by progressing the main story. Use a Copper Pickaxe to mine Iron Ore veins. Smelt it into Foothills Iron Ingots for all Lv2 Workbench recipes. Related: Iron Ore Locations & Uses Guide

faq.question: 19. What's the best early-game food?
faq.answer: Coconuts are the best early-game food. Harvest them from palm trees on beaches — they restore both hunger and thirst at the same time. Stockpile coconuts whenever you see palm trees.

faq.question: 20. How do I unlock more crafting recipes?
faq.answer: Some recipes only appear after you've collected the required materials for the first time. If a recipe isn't showing, try exploring new areas, mining different resources, or progressing the main story. Recipe visibility also depends on your Workbench level .

faq.question: Where is the best spot to farm Clay?
faq.answer: The starting island's riverbanks and shorelines are the best early-game spots. Look for large dark mud patches. The same deposits respawn over time.

faq.question: Can I collect Clay without a Pickaxe?
faq.answer: No, you need at least a Stone Pickaxe (3 Stone + 3 Wood at Workbench). Higher-tier pickaxes work faster.

faq.question: How much Clay do I need total?

faq.question: Where do I find Copper Ore in Windrose?
faq.answer: Copper Ore is found in Copper Deposit Mines marked by a pickaxe icon (⚒) on the map. These caves are located in the Coastal Jungle biome. Open your map, spot the pickaxe symbol, and travel to that location. Enter the cave with a Stone Pickaxe, torches, and a weapon.

faq.question: How do I smelt Copper Ore into Copper Ingots?
faq.answer: Place 6 Copper Ore + 1 Charcoal into the Smelting Furnace to produce 1 Copper Ingot . You must build the Smelting Furnace (15 Clay + 30 Stone) and Charcoal Kiln (25 Wood + 20 Clay) first. The Kiln produces Charcoal from Wood, which fuels the Furnace.

faq.question: What pickaxe do I need to mine Copper Ore?
faq.answer: You need the Stone Pickaxe (3 Stone + 3 Wood at Workbench Lv1). It is the first pickaxe you can craft and works on both Clay and Copper Ore. A Copper Pickaxe or better also works, but by then you already have copper access.

faq.question: Are there enemies inside Copper Deposit Mines?
faq.answer: Yes. Drowned enemies inhabit Copper Deposit Mines. They are hostile melee attackers. Bring a weapon (sword or axe), torches for visibility, and food for healing. Clear all enemies before mining to avoid being attacked mid-swing.

faq.question: How many Copper Ore deposits are in one cave?
faq.answer: Each Copper Deposit Mine contains 8 to 15 Poor Copper Ore deposits . With the 6:1 smelting ratio, one full cave clear yields roughly 1–3 Copper Ingots . You will need to visit multiple caves or re-visit after respawn to craft a full set of copper tools.

faq.question: Do Copper Ore deposits respawn?
faq.answer: Yes, Copper Ore deposits inside mines do respawn after a period of in-game time. Mark the cave entrance on your map so you can return for repeat farming runs. Respawning makes it possible to farm Copper indefinitely from the same mine.

faq.question: What is the most important resource in Windrose?
faq.answer: Copper Ore is the most critical early-game resource. It unlocks Copper tools, Copper Nails for storage expansion, and the entire metal tool progression chain. Your first priority after crafting a Stone Pickaxe should be locating a Copper Deposit Mine—marked by a pickaxe icon on the map in the Coastal Jungle biome.

faq.question: Which pickaxe do I need for each ore?
faq.answer: Stone Pickaxe mines Clay and Copper Ore. Copper Pickaxe is required for Iron Ore. Iron Pickaxe is required for Sulfur. Each ore tier demands the pickaxe one tier below it—you cannot skip ahead.

faq.question: How many resources do I need for the Smelting Furnace?
faq.answer: The Smelting Furnace costs 15 Clay + 30 Stone . You should also craft the Charcoal Kiln ( 25 Wood + 20 Clay ) at the same time, as the Kiln produces the Charcoal fuel needed to run the Furnace. Budget at least 35 Clay total for both structures.

faq.question: Can I get Gunpowder without crafting it?
faq.answer: Yes. In the early game, Gunpowder is found in the Smuggler’s Treasure cave on the first island (10 Gunpowder + 4 Rum in a chest behind breakable wood piles guarded by Drowned enemies). Pirate Camps may also drop Gunpowder as loot. Late-game crafting at the Millstone provides a renewable source.

faq.question: What should I gather first when starting Windrose?
faq.answer: Start with Wood and Stone to craft a Stone Pickaxe and Stone Axe. Then gather Clay from dark mud patches near water on the starting island—you need 35+ Clay for the Kiln and Furnace. After those structures are built, head to a Copper Deposit Mine for Copper Ore .

faq.question: Where do I find Iron Ore in Windrose?
faq.answer: Iron Ore is found in the Foothills region , accessed after progressing the main questline northward from the Coastal Jungle. Look for Iron Ore veins —dark metallic streaks on rocky surfaces—throughout the Foothills. Veins are scattered on exposed rock, not concentrated in caves like Copper.

faq.question: What pickaxe do I need for Iron Ore?
faq.answer: You need a Copper Pickaxe (2 Copper Ingots + 3 Wood at Workbench). The Stone Pickaxe cannot mine Iron Ore. Smelt Copper Ore first, craft the Copper Pickaxe, then head to the Foothills.

faq.question: What is the smelting ratio for Iron Ore?
faq.answer: The Iron smelting ratio is 6 Iron Ore + 2 Charcoal = 1 Foothills Iron Ingot . This is twice the Charcoal cost of Copper smelting (which uses 1 Charcoal). Stockpile extra Charcoal before starting Iron smelting batches.

faq.question: What can I craft with Foothills Iron Ingots?
faq.answer: Foothills Iron Ingots unlock all Lv2 Workbench recipes : the Anvil (station upgrade), Iron Pickaxe, Iron Axe, Iron Sword, Iron Armor pieces (Chestplate, Leggings, Helmet), Iron Bullets (ammunition), and the Explorer Backpack (largest inventory upgrade).

faq.question: Do I need to build the Anvil to use Iron Ingots?
faq.answer: Some basic Iron tools (Pickaxe, Axe) can be crafted directly at the Workbench. However, the Anvil (3 Foothills Iron Ingot + 5 Stone) is required to unlock Lv2 weapons and armor recipes . Build it early in your Iron progression.

faq.question: How many Iron Ore veins are in the Foothills?
faq.answer: The Foothills region contains 15–25 Iron Ore veins scattered across rocky terrain. Veins are spread out rather than clustered, so thorough exploration is required. Veins respawn over time, making the Foothills a renewable Iron source.

items.title: Windrose Brigantine Guide: Balanced Versatile Ship — Stats, Build & Strategy (2026)
items.description: Complete Windrose Brigantine ship guide. The most versatile ship in the game with balanced speed, firepower, and armor. Best ship for boss encounters and group play. Updated for 2026.
items.h1: Windrose Brigantine Guide: Balanced Versatile Ship — Stats, Build & Strategy (2026)

faq.question: Is the Brigantine the best ship in Windrose?
faq.answer: The Brigantine is the most versatile ship and the recommended choice for most content. It offers the best balance of speed, firepower, and armor, making it effective in nearly every situation. While specialized ships excel in specific roles (Sloop for speed, Frigate for raw power), the Brigantine never feels like the wrong choice.

faq.question: What crew size is best for the Brigantine?
faq.answer: A 3-player crew is the sweet spot for the Brigantine. This allows one helmsman, one dedicated gunner, and one repair/boarding specialist. The ship can accommodate up to 4 crew members for added flexibility — the fourth slot works well as a dedicated boarding fighter.

faq.question: Can the Brigantine be used solo?
faq.answer: The Brigantine can be operated solo but is less effective than the Sloop for solo play. Managing a larger ship alone means you cannot fully utilize all cannon ports simultaneously, and repairs take longer. For dedicated solo play, the Sloop is recommended, but solo Brigantine is viable if you want more firepower at the cost of speed.

faq.question: How do I unlock the Brigantine?
faq.answer: The Brigantine becomes available at shipyards after progressing through the early-game story and defeating the second boss (or accumulating sufficient resources through alternative means). It requires a significant investment of gold and materials compared to the Sloop.

items.title: Windrose Frigate Guide: Heavy Warship — Max Firepower, Stats & Build (2026)
items.description: Complete Windrose Frigate ship guide. The heaviest warship with maximum firepower and armor. Best for endgame fleet combat, large crews, and tanking boss encounters. Updated for 2026.
items.h1: Windrose Frigate Guide: Heavy Warship — Max Firepower, Stats & Build (2026)

faq.question: Is the Frigate worth the slow speed?
faq.answer: Yes, for endgame content and fleet combat, the Frigate's overwhelming firepower and durability more than compensate for its slow speed. In situations where you can position before engaging — such as defending a port or fighting a stationary boss — the Frigate excels. However, for exploration and solo play, the slow speed can be frustrating, and the Sloop or Brigantine is more enjoyable.

faq.question: How many crew members does the Frigate need?
faq.answer: The Frigate supports 4-6 crew members. A minimum of 4 is recommended for basic operation — any fewer and you cannot manage cannons, repairs, and sailing simultaneously. The ideal crew is 5-6: one helmsman, two gunners (one per broadside), one dedicated repair crew, and one to two boarding fighters.

faq.question: Can the Frigate be used for boss fights?
faq.answer: The Frigate can be used for boss fights, particularly against bosses that rely on sustained damage rather than fast projectile patterns. Against tank-style bosses like Blackbeard, the Frigate's armor and firepower are ideal. However, for bosses like Charon's Obols with heavy dodge requirements in Phase 2 (Obol Storm), the slow speed is a significant liability. The Brigantine is generally safer for most boss encounters.

faq.question: How do I unlock the Frigate?
faq.answer: The Frigate is an endgame ship unlocked after completing the main story or accumulating significant late-game resources. It requires rare materials from boss drops (including Charon's Obols ), a large gold investment, and a shipyard capable of constructing heavy warships. Expect to invest heavily before your Frigate is combat-ready.

faq.question: Can I use the Frigate for trading?
faq.answer: Yes, the Frigate has the largest cargo capacity of any ship, making it excellent for bulk trading. However, its slow speed means trade routes take longer. For high-value, time-sensitive trade runs, a Brigantine may offer better profit per hour. Use the Frigate for low-value, high-volume cargo where capacity matters more than speed.

faq.question: Is the Sloop good for solo play?
faq.answer: Yes, the Sloop is the best ship for solo players in Windrose. Its small crew requirement (only 1 crew member needed), high speed, and maneuverability make it ideal for solo exploration, hit-and-run tactics, and escaping dangerous encounters that would overwhelm a lone player on a larger ship.

faq.question: Can the Sloop defeat bosses?
faq.answer: The Sloop can handle early-game bosses but struggles against mid-to-late game encounters like Charon's Obols . Its low armor and firepower make prolonged engagements risky. For serious boss fights, the Brigantine or Frigate is recommended.

faq.question: How do I upgrade the Sloop?
faq.answer: Prioritize sail improvements for maximum speed and turning, then cannon upgrades for better hit-and-run damage. Hull reinforcements should be your last priority — the Sloop's defense is its speed, not its durability. Visit the shipyard at any major port to access upgrade options.

faq.question: Can I have multiple ships?
faq.answer: Yes, you can own multiple ships and switch between them at any port. Many players keep a Sloop for exploration and solo play while maintaining a Brigantine or Frigate for group content and boss encounters.

faq.question: Which recipe increases inventory space?
faq.answer: Torn Sailcloth Bag is the first storage upgrade, followed later by Sailor Backpack and Bosun Backpack.

faq.question: Where are the full recipes?
faq.answer: Use the Workbench Recipes , Smelting , and crafting subcategory pages.

items.h1: Windrose Armor Sets Guide: Complete List (2026)

faq.question: What is the best armor in Windrose?
faq.answer: The Iron Armor Set currently provides the highest defense rating in Windrose. It requires Iron Ingots and access to late-game mining locations. For mid-game, the Copper Armor Set is the best available upgrade from the starter Survivor's Set.

faq.question: How do I upgrade from the Survivor's Set?
faq.answer: Craft the Copper Armor Set as your first upgrade. You'll need Copper Ingots from smelting Copper Ore, plus workbench access. Each piece (head, chest, legs) must be crafted individually. Iron Armor becomes available once you reach Iron Ore deposits.

faq.question: Does armor have set bonuses?
faq.answer: Current community testing has not confirmed set bonuses for wearing a full matching set. The benefit of full sets is simply maximizing your defense in every slot. This may change in future updates.

faq.question: Can I repair damaged armor?
faq.answer: Armor durability and repair mechanics are still being investigated. Based on the Soulslite design philosophy, armor likely has durability that can be repaired at a Workbench using the same materials used to craft it.

faq.question: What is the best melee weapon in Windrose?
faq.answer: The Saber is the best overall melee weapon for its balanced damage, speed, and stamina efficiency. The Rapier excels for crit-focused DPS builds, while the Club is preferred for stagger-locking enemies.

faq.question: How does ammo progression work in Windrose?
faq.answer: Ammo progression goes from Stone Bullet (starter) to Copper Bullet (mid-game) to Iron Bullet (late-game). Each tier deals significantly more damage and requires the corresponding ingot plus gunpowder to craft.

faq.question: Which armor set should I use as a beginner?
faq.answer: The Survivor's Set is the starter armor in Windrose. It provides basic protection and is automatically available. Upgrade to crafted copper or iron armor as soon as you can smelt ingots.

faq.question: Can I use melee and ranged weapons together?
faq.answer: Yes. Windrose lets you equip a melee weapon and a ranged weapon simultaneously. A common strategy is to open with a Musket shot at range, then switch to Saber or Rapier for close combat.

faq.question: Are tier rankings final?
faq.answer: No. Windrose is in Early Access and balance patches are frequent. Tier rankings reflect the current patch and community consensus. Check back after major updates.

faq.question: What is the best melee weapon for beginners in Windrose?
faq.answer: The Saber is the best melee weapon for beginners. It has balanced damage, moderate speed, and reasonable stamina cost, making it forgiving while you learn enemy attack patterns and dodge timing.

faq.question: How do I stagger enemies with melee weapons?
faq.answer: Blunt weapons like the Club build stagger (poise damage) faster than bladed weapons. Land consecutive hits to break an enemy's poise meter. Halberds also deal high stagger on heavy attacks. Staggered enemies are briefly stunned and take bonus damage.

faq.question: What is the attack pattern for melee combat in Windrose?
faq.answer: The fundamental melee pattern is: dodge the enemy attack, land 1-2 quick hits , then retreat or dodge again. Greedy combos of 3+ hits will drain your stamina and leave you vulnerable to counter-attacks. Prioritize survival over damage.

faq.question: Should I use a shield with melee weapons?
faq.answer: Windrose does not currently feature dedicated shields. Defense comes from dodge rolling , positioning, and armor. The "block" is effectively your dodge invincibility frames. Invest in learning dodge timing rather than looking for a shield option.

faq.question: Musket or Blunderbuss: which ranged weapon is better?
faq.answer: The Musket is better for long-range sniping and boss fights due to its high single-shot damage and accuracy. The Blunderbuss excels in close-quarters against groups with its spread shot. Most players carry the Musket as their primary ranged option and switch to Blunderbuss for ship boarding or dungeon runs.

faq.question: Where do I get gunpowder in Windrose?
faq.answer: Gunpowder is found in Smuggler Stashes (hidden caches around the map), Pirate Camp drops (loot from defeated pirates), and can occasionally be found in coastal cave chests and shipwrecks. It cannot be crafted directly, so stockpile every source you find.

faq.question: How do I craft bullets in Windrose?
faq.answer: Bullets are crafted at the Workbench. Stone Bullet: Stone + Gunpowder. Copper Bullet: Copper Ingot + Gunpowder (requires Smelting Furnace). Iron Bullet: Iron Ingot + Gunpowder (requires Smelting Furnace and Iron Ore access).

faq.question: Do bullets carry over between weapon types?
faq.answer: Yes. Both the Musket and Blunderbuss draw from the same ammo pool. You do not need separate ammunition types for different ranged weapons, but weapon damage scaling still applies.
